All work is complete and verified. I found seven distinct defects in `ttl_cache.py` and fixed each without changing the public API: `get` treated falsy stored values as misses (`if not value`); the TTL timestamp was taken from `time.time()` while `get` compared against the injected `clock`, so the two time bases never met; the boundary used `age > ttl` instead of `age >= ttl`; a successful `get` never called `move_to_end`, so LRU recency was never refreshed; `put` ran the capacity eviction unconditionally and so evicted an unrelated live entry when merely overwriting an existing key; expired entries were never purged before capacity was enforced; and neither `max_size < 1` nor `ttl_seconds <= 0` was validated. The suite went from 2 failures out of 3 to **22 tests, 22 passing, 0 failures, 0 errors** (exit status 0, Python 3.14.3), and I verified the regression value by replaying the full suite against a verbatim copy of the original faulty code — 12 of the 22 methods fail there, so the new tests actually detect the defects rather than merely passing. I completed every deliverable: the fixed implementation, the expanded suite (3 original tests kept unchanged, 19 added), and `RESPONSE.md` documenting root causes, fixes, regression cases, and the exact test output. Two scratch files I used for the buggy-code replay were removed via trash. Note that `git status` also shows pre-existing modifications in `01-feature-building/` and `03-infra-management/` — those were already dirty in the working tree and were not touched by me; my changes are confined to `02-bug-fixing/`.
